q-224481.name: Question 1
q-224481.worked_solution:
The cumulative distribution function of a discrete random variable $X$ is a function $F(x)$ such that

$$
F(x)=P(X\le x).
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X<10) & =P(X\in \{0,1,…,9\}) \\  & =P(X\le 9) \\  & =F(9) \\  & =0.3405.\end{aligned}
$$

q-224486.name: Question 2
q-224486.worked_solution:
The cumulative distribution function of a discrete random variable $X$ is a function $F(x)$ such that

$$
F(x)=P(X\le x).
$$

So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}F(5) & =P(X\le 5) \\  & =P(X\in \{0,1,…,5\}) \\  & =P(X\in \{0,1,2\})+P(X\in \{3,4,5\}) \\  & =P(X\le 2)+P(2<X\le 5) \\  & =F(2)+P(2<X\le 5).\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}P(2<X\le 5) & =F(5)-F(2) \\  & =0.4457-0.0620 \\  & =0.3837.\end{aligned}
$$

Using the cumulative distribution function table of the Poisson random variable X∼Po(6) given below, compute P(2<X≤5).

x 2 3 4 5 6 7 8
P(X≤x) 0.0620 0.1512 0.2851 0.4457 0.6063 0.7440 0.8472
a
0.4457
b
0.4040
c
0.3212
d
0.3837
e
0.6063
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The cumulative distribution function of a discrete random variable X is a function F(x) such that

F(x)=P(X≤x).

So, we have

F(5)=P(X≤5)=P(X∈{0,1,…,5})=P(X∈{0,1,2})+P(X∈{3,4,5})=P(X≤2)+P(2<X≤5)=F(2)+P(2<X≤5).

Therefore,

P(2<X≤5)=F(5)−F(2)=0.4457−0.0620=0.3837.

q-225086.name: Question 5
q-225086.worked_solution:
The cumulative distribution function of a discrete random variable $X$ is a function $F(x)$ such that

$$
F(x)=P(X\le x).
$$

To solve the given problem, we can use the rule

$$
P(X>a)=1-P(X\le a)=1-F(a).
$$

Now, note that 

$$
P(X\ge 8)=P(X>7).
$$

 

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X\ge 8) & =P(X>7) \\  & =1-P(X\le 7) \\  & =1-F(7) \\  & =1-0.3239 \\  & =0.6761.\end{aligned}
$$

fields.input_html: 0.6761

F(x)=P(X≤x).

Now, note that

P(X≥8)=P(X>7).

Therefore, we have

P(X≥8)=P(X>7)=1−P(X≤7)=1−F(7)=1−0.3239=0.6761.
